'''Jeremy John Wade''' (born 23 March 1956) is a British television presenter, biologist, [[Angling|angler]], adventurer and author. He is known for his wildlife documentary television series ''[[River Monsters]]'' (2009-2017) as well as ''Mighty Rivers'' and ''Dark Waters''.

== Early life ==
Jeremy Wade was born in [[Ipswich]] and brought up in [[Nayland]] where his father was a [[vicar]].<ref>{{cite web |author=gabba / CONTROL |url=http://www.tbivision.com/article.php?category=4&article=1026&page=2 |title=TBI – Television Business International – Article / Key strategic business information on the production, distribution, broadcasting and financing of TV programming around the world |publisher=Tbivision.com |access-date=1 June 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120426045939/http://www.tbivision.com/article.php?category=4&article=1026&page=2 |archive-date=26 April 2012 }}</ref> He attended [[Dean Close School]] and has a degree in [[zoology]] from [[Bristol University]] and a postgraduate teaching certificate in biological sciences from the [[University of Kent]]. He previously worked as a secondary school biology teacher in [[Kent]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.jeremywade.co.uk/journalism.html |title=travel, natural history & fishing journalist |publisher=Jeremy Wade |date=30 August 2008 |access-date=1 June 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120606001727/http://www.jeremywade.co.uk/journalism.html |archive-date=6 June 2012 }}</ref>

== Career ==
At a young age, Jeremy Wade became interested in fishing; he began as a child when he was living in [[East Anglia]], on the banks of Suffolk's [[River Stour, Suffolk|River Stour]]. "The village where I grew up had a river flowing through it. So it was inevitable, I think, that I should be drawn to it in the same way that people born in sight of Alpine peaks become climbers. My first attempts to catch fish, age seven or eight, were unsuccessful, but then I had some guidance from a school friend and after my first catch I never looked back. My parents were happy for me to stay out all day and a big part of my fishing was wanting to find new places, a process that has continued to this day."<ref name="Jeremy Wade: Exclusive Interview">{{cite journal|title=Jeremy Wade: Exclusive Interview|journal=Adventure Outdoors Magazine|issue=Summer 2016|page=72}}</ref>

In 1982, Wade made his first overseas trip, to [[India]]'s mountain rivers. Recalling this journey, Wade stated that trip was very hard going. "I took just £200 ($265.62 USD) to last me three months but I managed to catch some fish such as [[Himalayan mahseer]] up to 18 pounds". Upon his return to England, Wade wrote a couple of articles about his experiences in India for a fishing magazine. "Despite the discomfort of travelling at such a basic level, there was a real feeling of achievement and I immediately started saving money to go somewhere else. I wasn't sure where at that point but I knew there must be other exotic fish out there, although probably not as well documented as Mahseer, but possibly even more spectacular."<ref name="Jeremy Wade: Exclusive Interview"/>

It was during another journey to India in 2005 in the Himalayan foothills that the concept for the television series ''[[River Monsters]]'' first presented itself. Upon hearing of stories from locals that some people had gone missing in the river, Wade began investigating. "Locals believed the perpetrator was a giant fish. It had the potential for a fascinating TV show--not just for people interested in fish and fishing, but for everyone." The fish turned out to be the [[Bagarius yarrelli|Goonch catfish]], with Wade landing a 161-pound specimen in an epic battle for the episode.<ref name="Jeremy Wade: Exclusive Interview"/> He has taken many trips to the [[Congo (area)|Congo]] and [[Amazon rainforest]]s. With the aid of local fishermen, Wade travels the world to catch various fish. Wade published his first book, ''Somewhere Down the Crazy River'', with joint-author Paul Boote, in 1992.<ref name=JWbooks>{{cite web |url=http://www.jeremywade.co.uk/books.html |title=Books by Jeremy Wade |work=Jeremy Wade |date=1 November 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130419081514/http://www.jeremywade.co.uk/books.html |archive-date=19 April 2013 }}</ref><ref name=":1" /> Wade has also written ''River Monsters'' (2011),<ref name=JWbooks /><ref name=":2" /> which details his hunts and journeys around the world, and ''How to Think Like a Fish'' (2019)<ref name=":3" />, which combines Wade's past experiences with his ruminations on life.

Jeremy Wade made his acting debut in the 1986 [[Bollywood]] film [[Allah Rakha (film)|Allah Rakha]] playing an extra; he would later return to film in the 2014 film, ''[[Blood Lake (2014 film)|Blood Lake: Attack of the Killer Lampreys]]'', playing a [[lamprey]] expert.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=Banerjee|first=Sudeshna|date=15 July 2020|title=Jeremy Wade drops a fishing line deep into remote waters for his new show|url=https://www.telegraphindia.com/entertainment/jeremy-wade-drops-a-fishing-line-deep-into-remote-waters-for-his-new-show/cid/1786406|access-date=2020-10-04|website=The Telegraph|location=India}}</ref> He had previously covered the fish in the ''River Monsters'' episode "Vampires of the Deep".

When the ''River Monsters'' episode "Deep Sea Demons" aired in 2016, Wade officially became known as one of the very few people in history to witness a live, healthy [[oarfish]].<ref>{{cite AV media |people=[[Jeremy Wade]] |date=18 April 2023 |title=Jeremy Wade's Incredible Encounter with Rare Deep Ocean Fish |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pfzrD4akqxQ |trans-title= |format=Video |work= |type= |language=English |location=YouTube |publisher=River Monsters |time=7:24 |access-date=1 April 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite episode |credits= |last=Wade |first=Jeremy |date=April 7, 2016 |title=Deep Sea Demon|series=River Monsters |season=8 |number=1 |language=en |publisher=Icon Films |minutes=38:34 |network=Animal Planet}}</ref>

In 2016, while filming on a remote island near Australia, Wade and his crew stumbled upon a man who had become stranded on the island after losing his boat while digging for oysters. The man, identified as Tremaine, had been stranded on the island for two days before Wade and his crew found him.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://wtop.com/tv/2016/04/river-monsters-crew-catches-real-life-castaway/|title='River Monsters' crew catches real-life castaway|date=2016-04-21|work=WTOP|access-date=2018-05-02|archive-date=24 April 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160424020731/https://wtop.com/tv/2016/04/river-monsters-crew-catches-real-life-castaway/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Part of this incident was aired during the ''River Monsters'' episode "Death Down Under" (48th episode of the series), but after Wade's crew rehydrated the man, one crew member took the man for medical care while Wade and the rest of the crew continued their investigation.<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KQrxy065ZtI |title=TV Crew Miraculously Saves Man Stranded On Desert Island |date=2017-09-05 |last=Wade |first=Jeremy |publisher=River Monsters |access-date=2026-04-25 |via=YouTube}}</ref><ref>{{Cite episode |credits= |last=Wade |first=Jeremy |date=14 April 2016|series=River Monsters |title=Death Down Under |season=8 |number=2| language=en |publisher=Icon Films |network=Animal Planet}}</ref>

In 2018, Wade was recruited to host the [[Animal Planet]] documentary series ''Mighty Rivers'', in which he investigates the disappearance of freshwater giants from the world's most iconic rivers.<ref>{{Cite web|date=5 March 2018|title=Jeremy Wade Returns To Animal Planet in All-New Series "Jeremy Wade's Mighty Rivers"|url=https://corporate.discovery.com/discovery-newsroom/jeremy-wade-returns-to-animal-planet-in-all-new-series-jeremy-wades-mighty-rivers/|access-date=2020-10-04|website=corporate.discovery.com}}</ref> In 2019, Wade would go on to the Animal Planet documentary series ''Dark Waters'', which explored unexplained sightings of mythical beasts across the world.<ref name=":0" /> In 2020, he began a new TV series, ''Mysteries of the Deep'', where he explores underwater mysteries, ranging from the [[Loch Ness Monster]] to the [[Bermuda Triangle]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Charm|first=Neil|date=30 June 2020|title=Jeremy Wade checks out the Bermuda Triangle in new show|url=https://www.bworldonline.com/jeremy-wade-checks-out-the-bermuda-triangle-in-new-show/|access-date=2020-10-04|website=BusinessWorld}}</ref>

== Personal life ==

At various times during his journeys abroad, he has caught [[malaria]], been threatened at gunpoint, and survived a plane crash.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jeremy Wade|url=http://animal.discovery.com/tv-shows/river-monsters/bios/jeremy-wade.htm|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130116043918/http://animal.discovery.com/tv-shows/river-monsters/bios/jeremy-wade.htm|archive-date=16 January 2013|work=River Monsters|publisher=Discovery Corporation|quote=During these journeys he caught malaria, was arrested for spying, narrowly escaped drowning and survived a plane crash.}}</ref> He is fluent in [[Brazilian Portuguese|Portuguese]], which he studied during the many years he spent fishing in [[Brazil]], and also speaks [[French language|French]], [[Spanish language|Spanish]], and some Mandarin.
